findings.claim: EcoVerse is a sustainability-focused web application offering product barcode scanning, carbon footprint tracking, recyclability insights, eco-points, and community leaderboards.
The project addresses consumer difficulty in understanding the environmental impact and disposal guidance of everyday consumer products.
Features include real-time barcode scanning via ZXing and html5-qrcode, carbon emission estimation, recyclability analysis, gamified eco-points and badge rewards, and user leaderboards.
The technical stack consists of Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript 5, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, Firebase Auth, MongoDB/Mongoose, and a secondary Python FastAPI service with SQLAlchemy and SQLite.

The application architecture pairs Next.js middleware-protected frontend and API routes with a separate stateful Python FastAPI service (`ai_services/main.py`) for backend carbon analytics and leaderboard computations.
The repository provides containerization using a multi-stage Dockerfile based on `node:20-alpine` with non-root runtime execution and built-in health checking.

Next.js middleware and next.config.ts enforce strict security headers, including Content-Security-Policy (CSP), Permissions-Policy, X-Frame-Options, and X-Content-Type-Options, backed by Jest unit tests in middleware.csp.test.ts.
The Python FastAPI service file `ai_services/main.py` contains incomplete placeholder slots (`___`) in `get_user_profile`, which would cause syntax errors if executed.
The package name in `package.json` is set to 'my-v0-project', indicating project generation from a v0 boilerplate.
The application exhibits database architecture fragmentation, utilizing MongoDB with Mongoose on the Node.js side and SQLite with SQLAlchemy in the Python AI services directory.
A custom utility script `fix.js` is included to run regex modifications across source code files for console logs, TypeScript type annotations, and Tailwind configuration imports.
Complete React component implementation source files under `app/` and `components/` are omitted from the supplied context.
